req.title: Return 405 for unsupported /players root method
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using DELETE on /players/ (collection).

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-036 requires HTTP 405 when DELETE is issued against the /players/ collection endpoint. The router defines DELETE only at /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}, not at /players/. FastAPI/Starlette will return 405 Method Not Allowed when a registered path receives an unsupported HTTP method. Three tests are needed: (1) positive – DELETE /players/ returns exactly 405 (EP, primary requirement path); (2) negative – GET /players/ returns 200, confirming the collection path itself is alive and the 405 is method-specific, not a routing blackhole (NEG + DT); (3) boundary – verify the Allow header in the 405 response does NOT include DELETE, and that adjacent supported methods (POST, GET) on /players/ still return non-405 codes (BVA + comparison-mutation). Each test uses fastapi.testclient.TestClient in-process, asserts exact status codes, and avoids any invented attributes.

tests.name: test_delete_players_collection_returns_405
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
DELETE /players/ is not registered as a route handler
Database is pre-loaded with 26 player rows
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 405
trace: R-PLAYER-036: system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using DELETE on /players/ (collection)
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_players_collection_returns_405():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    response = client.delete('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 405

test_delete_players_collection_returns_405()

trace: R-PLAYER-036: confirms 405 is method-specific; GET on same path must succeed

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_get_players_collection_returns_200_not_405():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    response = client.get('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.status_code != 405
    body = response.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)

test_get_players_collection_returns_200_not_405()

tests.name: test_delete_players_collection_405_allow_header_excludes_delete
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
Starlette returns Allow header on 405 responses
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
Inspect response status code and Allow header
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 405
Allow header is present in the response
Allow header does not contain DELETE
Allow header contains GET and/or POST
trace: R-PLAYER-036: 405 must be returned; Allow header must not advertise DELETE on collection
BVA: boundary between allowed and disallowed methods on /players/
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_players_collection_405_allow_header_excludes_delete():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    response = client.delete('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 405
    allow = response.headers.get('allow', '')
    allow_upper = allow.upper()
    assert 'DELETE' not in allow_upper
    assert 'GET' in allow_upper or 'POST' in allow_upper

test_delete_players_collection_405_allow_header_excludes_delete()

tests.name: test_post_players_collection_not_405
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
POST /players/ is a registered route handler
Database is pre-loaded with 26 player rows
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
Issue POST request to /players/ with a valid new player payload (squadNumber 99)
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 201
Response body contains the created player with squadNumber 99
trace: R-PLAYER-036: POST on /players/ must not be affected; only DELETE must yield 405
DT: decision table row where method=POST -> allowed; method=DELETE -> 405
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_post_players_collection_not_405():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    payload = {
        'firstName': 'Test',
        'lastName': 'Player',
        'squadNumber': 99,
        'position': 'Goalkeeper'
    }
    response = client.post('/players/', json=payload)
    assert response.status_code == 201
    assert response.status_code != 405
    body = response.json()
    assert body['squadNumber'] == 99

test_post_players_collection_not_405()

tests.name: test_delete_players_collection_405_response_is_not_2xx
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
DELETE /players/ is not a registered route
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
Assert status code is not in the 2xx range and is exactly 405
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 405
trace: R-PLAYER-036: error pathway is HTTP 405; expected outcome (2xx) must NOT occur
NEG: catches mutations that change 405 to 200/201/204 or suppress the method check
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_players_collection_405_response_is_not_2xx():
    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
    response = client.delete('/players/')
    assert response.status_code == 405
    assert response.status_code != 200
    assert response.status_code != 201
    assert response.status_code != 204
    assert response.status_code != 404

test_delete_players_collection_405_response_is_not_2xx()
